rows: Ethylene acrylic elastomer. Our signature compound, supplied to Mahindra & Mahindra for engine and transmission applications. Holds compression-set stability where oil, heat and ozone act together.
Fluorocarbon rubber, the first choice for aggressive chemical environments. Resists petroleum oils, fuels and many solvents at sustained high temperature.
Nitrile butadiene rubber, the general-purpose industry standard. Outstanding resistance to petroleum oils and hydraulic fluids at moderate temperature.
Ethylene propylene diene rubber, the preferred material for water, steam and brake fluid service, with excellent weather and ozone resistance. Not for petroleum oils.
Vinyl methyl silicone, the widest service range of the eight. Biocompatible grades available. Poor abrasion resistance — not a wear part.
Polychloroprene. Balanced properties across weather, refrigerants and moderate oil exposure, and the family we reach for when flame retardancy is specified.
Styrene butadiene rubber. Abrasion resistance at low cost, for static seals in water and mild service. Not for oil or fuel contact.
Polyisoprene. The highest resilience of the eight, specified where a seal also has to damp. Not for oil, fuel or sustained heat.
A PTFE jacket over an FKM or silicone core — the chemical resistance of PTFE with the recovery of an elastomer. Specified where a compound would be attacked but a rigid seal cannot follow the groove.

fields.label: PTFE — two questions
paragraphs: One question, and it is a process question rather than a value. Encapsulated or solid? — PTFE-encapsulated O-rings (a PTFE jacket over an elastomer core) are a moulder’s product and fit what Margo does. Solid PTFE O-rings are machined from stock, not moulded, and are a different process with different equipment. The panel above is written for encapsulated. If Margo machines solid PTFE, the copy changes and so does the capability claim.

Temperature and hardness — standard published values. An encapsulated ring is a PTFE (FEP or PFA) jacket over an elastomer core, and the figures come from the core and the jacket together. Published practice: silicone core, FEP jacket −60 to +205 °C; FKM core, FEP jacket −20 to +205 °C; silicone core, PFA jacket −60 to +260 °C. Hardness runs 85–90 Shore A on a silicone core and 90–95 on FKM, because the jacket dominates — which is why an encapsulated ring needs a wider groove and more closure force than a plain elastomer ring of the same section. The table publishes the silicone-core figures, −60 to +205 °C at 85–95 Shore A, as the widest band Margo would quote against; state the core on the enquiry and the range narrows accordingly.
